newsitem.title: USA: February housing starts strongest in nearly 3 years.
newsitem.headline: February housing starts strongest in nearly 3 years.

text.p: Builders broke ground on new homes and apartments at the fastest clip in nearly three years during February, the Commerce Department said on Tuesday, bouncing back from severe weather in January.

Total starts shot up 12.2 percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.53 million in February -- the strongest building pace since 1.56 million in March 1994 -- after a revised 0.7 percent gain in January.
Building activity was much more robust in February than anticipated by Wall Street analysts, who had forecast housing starts at a rate of 1.45 million a year.
Previously, the department said January starts had risen 2 percent to a rate of 1.35 million but it revised that estimate.

The February pickup apparently reflected not only improved weather in much of the country after a severe January but also steady job gains as the economy completed a sixth consecutive year of expansion at the end of February.
The National Association of Home Builders said on Monday that its index of market activity rose in March and that the outlook for construction remained strong.

"All the market conditions are ripe for home buying," said Kent Colton, the association's executive vice president. "We've had a mild winter, a strong economy and relatively favourable interest rates."

The housing starts report confirmed that building activity was on a solid trajectory, which was indicated earlier when the Labour Department said there had been a huge 109,000 increase in construction industry jobs during February.
In addition, permit applications gained 3 percent in February to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.44 million, a sign that builders intend to keep up a strong building pace.

Construction starts on single-family homes climbed 8.8 percent in February to a rate of 1.22 million after rising 9.1 percent in January. Starts on apartments jumped 27.8 percent to a rate of 313,000 following a 25.5 percent drop in January.

Mortgage rates eased slightly in February from January. The Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp., or Freddie Mac, said rates for a 30-year loan averaged 7.65 percent in February, down from 7.82 percent in January.
The only region in which starts fell during February was the Northeast, where they were down 26.9 percent to a rate of 128,000 a year.

Starts soared 51.6 percent in the Midwest to 385,000 a year as weather improved in the region. In the South, building starts picked up 10.9 percent to a rate of 661,000 a year and in the West they increased 5 percent to an annual rate of 354,000.
